solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Be close by old rocker, ignorant

parts.note: nigh means near or close
a Ted (Teddy boy) was a 1950s rock-and-roll fan

explanation.surface: Someone sits near an ageing rock fan and proves clueless.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy, or Ted, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style clothes who followed rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Benighted describes someone in intellectual or moral darkness, lacking knowledge.

clue.text: Songs offered by a daughter in dances

indicators.note: in says the two small pieces go inside the word for dances

parts.note: balls are formal dances
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A girl sings songs at the dances.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrative folk songs or slow sentimental pop songs are kinds of song.

clue.text: See one getting upset, concealing twitching

indicators.note: concealing says those jumbled letters hide the other piece inside them
upset says the letters of the word one are knocked into a new order

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitching

explanation.surface: A person gets distressed while trying to hide a nervous twitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles the clue word into NOE, and 'concealing' has that jumble hide the twitch inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe or spot something is to see it.

clue.text: Gather good healthy meat?

parts.note: lean meat has little fat and so is healthy

explanation.surface: Collect some wholesome, low-fat meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To collect bit by bit, like information or leftover grain, is to gather.

clue.text: A honeyeater in perpetuity

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A bird that lives for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: The tui is a New Zealand bird of the honeyeater family, feeding on nectar.

clue.text: Unpleasant bird, sea eagle flying about

indicators.note: flying about says the letters of these words dart around into a new order

explanation.surface: A nasty bird of prey circling overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nasty or not to one's liking is unpleasant.

clue.text: Greek character not quite willing to get degree

indicators.note: not quite says the word for willing loses its final letter

parts.note: game means willing, up for it
an MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A Greek person, only half-keen, goes off to earn a qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: The third letter of the Greek alphabet is one of its characters.

clue.text: Lose a job and prepare to send out messages in December?

definitions.meaning: to be dismissed and handed back your employment papers

definitions.text: prepare to send out messages in December?
definitions.meaning: collecting Christmas greetings ready to post

explanation.surface: Being sacked just as the Christmas post is due.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, a sacked employee was handed their National Insurance cards; the second reading is buying Christmas cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be fired, and literally to acquire greetings for the festive season.

clue.text: Maiden takes horse-drawn vehicle, heading off for match

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: heading off says the vehicle word loses its first letter

parts.note: a carriage is pulled by horses

explanation.surface: A young woman rides in a coach to her wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A union of two people is a match, as in a good match.

clue.text: Stories about water mammals in chancy endeavours

indicators.note: about means the word for stories goes round the other piece

parts.note: lies are made-up stories
the otter is a water-loving mammal; the singular gives the letters needed

explanation.surface: Tall tales about otters are a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'mammals' is loose: only one of the animals is needed inside the fibs.
explanation.definitionFit: Draws and raffles decided purely by luck are risky ventures dependent on chance.

clue.text: Some pretty, rolling territory in Europe

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A description of lovely rolling hill country somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is an Alpine region spanning Austria and northern Italy.

clue.text: Moving up when about to come to conclusion

parts.note: as can mean when (as I left)
C is short for circa, about
an ending is a conclusion

explanation.surface: Climbing just as one is about to reach a decision.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to rise or climb, so the participle means going upward.

clue.text: One church hospital overlooking river, a cold building

indicators.note: in a down clue, overlooking puts the earlier pieces above the river

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
CE is the Church of England
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A chilly building set beside a church and hospital above a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Before refrigerators, a structure for storing ice was a deliberately cold store.

clue.text: Pass first of exams, then blunder

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word exams

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or blunder

explanation.surface: A student gets through the first exam and then makes a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to pass or slip by, as when weeks go by unnoticed.

clue.text: Something mucky reported in this country?

indicators.note: reported says the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: greasy describes something oily and mucky

explanation.surface: A question about a filthy story being spread round a country.
explanation.walkthrough: GREECE is said like GREASY in a non-rhotic accent: 'Something mucky' supplies the adjective said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean nation, its name referred to by 'this country' in the clue.

clue.text: Regard repose as protection for muscle

indicators.note: as protection for says the word for repose wraps round the muscle word

parts.note: rest is repose
a pec is a chest muscle, short for pectoral

explanation.surface: Valuing rest as a way of protecting your muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem or high regard for someone is the same as respect.

clue.text: Compassionate article penned by philosopher

indicators.note: penned by says the article is enclosed by the philosopher

parts.note: David Hume was a Scottish philosopher
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A kindly piece written by a philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing kindness and mercy toward others is being compassionate.

clue.text: Box with crazy old jokes?

parts.note: a chest is a large box
nuts means crazy

explanation.surface: A trunk full of mad, tired gags.
explanation.definitionFit: A stale joke or story told too often is called an old chestnut.

clue.text: Weapon bringing shock and awful tears

indicators.note: awful says the letters of tears are put into a bad, jumbled order

explanation.surface: A stun gun causes a jolt and dreadful crying.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electroshock stun gun used by police.

clue.text: Fruit black and dead

parts.note: the plum is a fruit
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A dark fruit that has gone off completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean exactly or precisely as adverbs, as in hitting the target dead centre.

clue.text: Bring back soldiers to home, say

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
in means at home
to state is to say

explanation.surface: An order to return troops to their homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone to a former post or position is to bring them back.

clue.text: I had to introduce a princess in the theatre

indicators.note: to introduce says the I-had contraction comes first, leading into the letter a

parts.note: I'd is short for I had

explanation.surface: Someone presents a princess on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Ida is the title heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of a Savoy opera is a stage princess.

clue.text: Island in secret exploit

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A clandestine operation on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest Greek island lies in the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Waits in street least cloudy at night

indicators.note: in says the word for waits goes inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: tarries means waits or lingers

explanation.surface: Someone lingers outside on the clearest night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waits' looks like carol singers (waits), but it is the verb, giving TARRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The most star-filled sky is the clearest one after dark, with the least cloud cover.
